terra.problem: Saying David starts with mercy because he is in Philistine hands supplies a reason the text does not give.
David says his enemies pursue him all day, not that they never take breaks.
The claim that David runs to the wilderness elsewhere needs a reference.
The psalm does not say that praise is absent from the enemies' actions.
The psalm says the enemies twist David's words, not that they trust nothing he says.
The prayer does not establish that David leaves the matter in God's hands or does not take action himself.
The explanation identifies the nations with those who wrong David, a connection the passage does not explicitly make.
The verse does not say nobody is laughing at David. It says his enemies will retreat.
The verse mentions vows and thank offerings but does not explicitly say the offerings pay the vows.
